# Citation

Jiang, R., Sun, T., Song, D., and Li, J. J. (2022). Statistics or biology: the zero-inflation controversy about scRNA-seq data. *Genome Biology* 23:31. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-022-02601-5 (PDF p. 1).

# One-Sentence Summary

This study separates biological and non-biological zeros in scRNA-seq, evaluates protocol-dependent count distributions, simulates masked zeros, and benchmarks observed, imputed and binarized inputs for clustering, dimension reduction and differential-expression analysis (PDF pp. 1–24).

# Research Question

Are the many zeros in scRNA-seq measurements biological, technical or sampling artifacts, how does zero-inflation modeling depend on protocol, and how do zero-handling choices affect downstream analyses? This paraphrases the article’s objectives (PDF pp. 1–2).

# Biological System

The real-data analyses use human peripheral blood mononuclear-cell (PBMC) data generated by Drop-seq, 10x Genomics and Smart-seq2, with B cells, CD14+ monocytes, CD4+ T cells, cytotoxic T cells and natural killer cells (PDF pp. 2, 9–11).

# Study Design

The paper combines conceptual review, analysis of three real PBMC protocol data sets, simulation with scDesign2, masking experiments, and benchmarking with Monocle3 and Seurat (PDF pp. 1–2, 9–14). The work is not solely a narrative review.

# Data

Three benchmark PBMC data sets generated by 10x Genomics, Drop-seq and Smart-seq2 are analyzed. Synthetic data are generated from fitted gene-by-cell models, with the number of synthetic cells set equal to the number of real cells for each cell type (PDF pp. 9–12). The authors define the top 1500 genes with the largest estimated mean differences between CD4+ T cells and cytotoxic T cells as true DE genes (PDF p. 11).

# Methods

- Define biological, technical and sampling zeros and clarify dropout, excess-zero and zero-inflation terminology (PDF pp. 2–4, Tables 1–2).
- Fit Poisson, zero-inflated Poisson, negative-binomial and zero-inflated negative-binomial distributions to protocol-specific counts and select models by likelihood-ratio tests (PDF pp. 8–11, Figure 5).
- Train scDesign2 on the three PBMC data sets and generate non-zero-inflated synthetic data preserving real genes and gene–gene correlations (PDF pp. 11–12).
- Add non-biological zeros using five masking schemes and proportions `p = 0.1, ..., 0.9`; analyze data with Monocle3 and Seurat (PDF pp. 12–13, Figure 6).
- Benchmark clustering, dimension reduction and DE analysis using adjusted Rand index, F1 score, precision and recall; DE F1 scores use a 5% false-discovery rate (PDF pp. 12–15).

# Software and Versions

The simulation uses scDesign2. The masking benchmarks use Monocle3 R package version 0.2.3.0 and Seurat R package version 3.2.1. The paper also discusses MAST within Seurat’s DE workflow (PDF pp. 11–13).

# Important Parameters

The masking proportions are `p = 0.1` through `0.9`; the true DE set contains 1500 genes; clustering is evaluated with adjusted Rand index; DE performance uses F1 score, precision and recall at a 5% false-discovery rate (PDF pp. 11–14, Figure 6). The four fitted count distributions are Poisson, ZIP, NB and ZINB (PDF pp. 8–10).

# Inputs and Outputs

Inputs are protocol-specific PBMC count matrices, cell-type labels, fitted count distributions and masked or transformed count matrices. Outputs include selected statistical models, clustering assignments, dimension-reduction representations, DE-gene calls and performance metrics (PDF pp. 9–15).

# Main Results

Non-zero-inflated Poisson or negative-binomial distributions are selected for almost all genes in the 10x Genomics and Drop-seq data, whereas zero-inflated distributions are selected for about half of the genes in Smart-seq2 data (PDF pp. 9–11, Figure 5). Clustering accuracy is robust to masking up to `p = 0.6` for most schemes, with Seurat more robust than Monocle3; DE-gene identification is more sensitive to non-biological zeros (PDF pp. 12–14, Figure 6). The authors conclude that zero inflation is a statistical modeling property and does not directly identify biological zeros (PDF pp. 8–11).

# Assumptions

The simulation assumes that fitted scDesign2 models preserve relevant real genes and gene–gene correlations and that removing fitted zero-inflation components provides a useful positive-control data set (PDF pp. 11–12). The definition of true DE genes is based on estimated mean differences between two cell types (PDF p. 11).

# Limitations

Biological and non-biological zeros are difficult to distinguish without biological knowledge or spike-in controls. Masking schemes are simplified representations of zero-generation mechanisms, and the authors note that some schemes may be more or less realistic (PDF pp. 2, 12–15).

# Reproducible Implementation Details

Reported details include scDesign2, Monocle3 0.2.3.0, Seurat 3.2.1, four count distributions, five masking schemes, masking proportions 0.1–0.9, 1500 true DE genes and a 5% FDR. Exact input accession identifiers and complete scripts: Not reported (PDF pp. 9–14).

# Relevance to simitall

**Inference, not an author recommendation:** The paper could inform simitall provenance fields for zero-handling choices, protocol type, simulation parameters, masking schemes and evaluation metrics. It does not mention or evaluate simitall (PDF pp. 1–24).

# Terminology

- **Biological zero:** True absence of a gene’s transcripts in a cell (PDF pp. 2–4, Table 1).
- **Sampling zero:** Absence of observed reads or UMIs caused by inefficient amplification or limited sequencing depth (PDF p. 3, Table 1).
- **Zero inflation:** Proportion of zeros exceeding what is expected under a specified count model (PDF p. 4, Table 2).
- **UMI:** Unique molecular identifier used to correct amplification bias in non-zero measurements (PDF p. 3, Table 1).
